outroLine: Set it once — new order files import themselves.

beats.shot: Land on Settings → SFTP pull (?tab=sftp deep-link). Cursor settles on the card title, sweeps the subtitle, rests on the paid-plan notice.
beats.vo: When a system exports purchase orders to an S F T P server, ProcuLink can log in, pick up new files, and parse them — automatically, every few minutes. You set it up yourself, under Settings, S F T P pull, and it's included on every paid plan.

beats.shot: Cursor clicks Host and types sftp.nordic-electronics.example, rests on Port (22 stays), then clicks Remote directory and types /exports/orders — a beat of emphasis on the path field.
beats.vo: Give it the host, the port — 22 unless it was moved — and the absolute path to the folder to watch. That path is the single most common thing to get wrong.

beats.shot: Cursor types a username, then a password (rendered as dots), then rests on the 'Secrets are encrypted and never shown again' footer hint.
beats.vo: Then the credentials — the username and password for that server. Like every secret in ProcuLink, the password is encrypted at rest and never shown back.

beats.shot: Cursor touches the 'every few minutes' subtitle, then opens the Default supplier select and picks ElectroSupply Co; rests on the 'attributed to this supplier' helper line.
beats.vo: There's no schedule to tune — ProcuLink checks every few minutes on its own. It does need a default supplier, though, because a raw file drop carries no routing — every imported order is attributed to the supplier you pick here.

beats.shot: Calm sweep of the finished form: the polling toggle, down to the Save button (rested on, never clicked — saving has no mock backend), then the plan-hint footer.
beats.vo: Each poll imports only the files it hasn't seen before and records them, so nothing is re-imported. And ProcuLink never deletes or moves your files — the source folder is left exactly as the sender left it.

beats.shot: The honest failure: cursor returns to the Remote directory field and traces the typed path, then rests on the 'Need help? See the SFTP polling guide' link.
beats.vo: One thing to watch. A wrong path can still connect successfully — ProcuLink just finds an empty folder. No error, no orders. So if polling runs and nothing appears, re-check the exact path against where the source system actually writes. Reaching the server is not the same as finding files.
